title: Routes fixed by the space, carrying one bit at most
claim: Routes in the knot's spaces are fixed by the space and carry at most one bit. Let H be a knot's space. (1) Kinds of 3-edge cut: a nontrivial 3-edge cut is either a shift of a nontrivial 2-edge cut (one vertex carries two of its edges; removing that vertex from its shore leaves the 2-edge cut) or a proper splice cut (three distinct ports and three distinct slots); a shift is twisted iff the shore that absorbed the moved vertex accepts disequality across the 2-edge cut. (2) Fixed by the space: in ten knot's spaces the proper splice cuts are pairwise non-crossing and cross no 2-edge cut, and every crossing pair of nontrivial cuts involves a shift or two 2-edge cuts of one cycle of units; so the parts and the cuts between them form one decomposition determined by the incidence graph (unchanged under relabelling), and a route between two parts, through hubs or through 2-edge cuts, is fixed by the space, not chosen by an observer. (3) What routes carry: in a cycle of k Fano blocks (k = 3, 5, 7) an arc of m units accepts exactly x + y = m (mod 2) on its port colour and slot value; between two units there are exactly two routes, which carry opposite parities because k is odd, and the space fails because they disagree (the even cycle of 4 blocks, a control, is colourable and its routes agree). Across a proper splice cut each side acts as one point or one line whatever it contains (A), so a route through a hub carries nothing about what lies beyond it. (4) Separation: for every pair of units and every non-empty set J of junctions of the cycles of 3, 5 and 7 blocks, H with J's incidences cut is colourable, and the joint relation of the two units' port colours is a product exactly when J meets both routes; otherwise it is the parity of the route J leaves intact. (5) Counting the witnesses that relations quantify away, every Fano unit has 5 colourings for each accepted pair and an arc of m units 5^m (m <= 3 by enumeration), so a counted length exists, as a count of hidden witnesses rather than a relation. (6) Reading: every route between parts is a two-place parity (it identifies its two channels up to sign) or passes a hub (equality on three channels); neither is a complete contact, so under the program's definitions these are routes of a declared substrate, separable by cutting them, not native paths composed of complete contacts, and no relation along them gives an extended distance.
failure_conditions: A nontrivial 3-edge cut with a vertex carrying two of its edges that is not a shift of a nontrivial 2-edge cut.
A shift whose twist disagrees with the parity accepted by the shore that absorbed the moved vertex.
Two crossing proper splice cuts, or a proper splice cut crossing a 2-edge cut, in one of the ten spaces.
An arc of m units whose accepted relation is not x + y = m (mod 2).
A non-empty junction set whose cut leaves two units unrelated while it misses a route, or related while it meets both.
A Fano unit with other than 5 colourings for an accepted pair.
foundation_claim_scope: Routes, separation and counts in declared finite systems; no extended distance is constructed.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-01.
validation.status: checked: classification of every nontrivial 3-edge cut of ten knot's spaces, the twist rule, crossings, relabelling invariance, arc relations on cycles of 3, 5, 7 blocks, separation for every pair of units and every non-empty junction set, unit and arc counts, an even-cycle control; no human or external review
validation.novelty: The cactus of 2-edge cuts, laminar tight cuts and frustrated cycles are classical graph and matching theory; the knot's-space instances and the reading against the program's definitions are new here.
